source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

50015.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Lamoille County swung hard toward Phil Scott, the Republican, over Democrat Amanda Janoo. Kamala Harris carried it by 36 points in 2024; Scott won it by 12, 6,871 votes to 5,433, a 47-point move. That is the second-largest shift among Vermont's 14 counties, every one of which moved right, against a statewide move of 38 points and a typical county move of 37. Similar counties moved less: Addison 39 points, Windsor 38, Windham 23.

About 12,506 votes were cast, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Nationally the pattern ran the other way, with 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moving left.

50027.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Windsor County went from a 36-point Harris win in 2024 to a 2-point win for Scott over Janoo, 14,135 votes to 13,538. That 38-point move toward the Republicans matches the state's own 38-point shift and is close to the typical Vermont county's 37, ranking Windsor 8th of 14. Every Vermont county moved right, even as 2,673 of the 2,775 counties counted nationally moved left. All of the expected vote is in.

Turnout was 28,336 votes, 83% of the 34,018 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Addison moved slightly more, 39 points, and Washington moved 42 but stayed narrowly Democratic.

50003.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Bennington County went from a 23-point Harris win in 2024 to a 7-point margin for Republican Phil Scott over Democrat Amanda Janoo, 8,543 votes to 7,449. That is a 29-point move toward the Republicans, matching Scott's statewide margin exactly. All of the expected vote is counted.

Every Vermont county moved right, and Bennington's shift was among the smaller ones: third of 14, against a typical move of 37 points. Similar counties swung further, with Orange moving 33 points, Caledonia 33 and Grand Isle 50. Nationally, most counties moved left. Turnout here was 80% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

50021.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Rutland County went from a narrow Harris win in 2024, by 5 points, to a large win for Phil Scott over Amanda Janoo, 17,304 votes to 8,960, a margin of 31 points. That is a 36-point move toward the Republicans, close to the typical Vermont county's 37-point shift. All 14 counties moved right, and Rutland ranks seventh. Similar counties moved about as much: Franklin shifted 39 points, Caledonia 33 and Orleans 32. Nationally, most counties moved left.

About 26,827 votes were cast, 79% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

50011.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Franklin County went from a narrow Democratic edge to a wide Republican one. Harris carried it by 3 points in 2024; in 2026 Scott beat Janoo by 36, 14,274 votes to 6,574, with all of the expected vote counted. That is a 39-point swing toward the Republicans, slightly more than the state's 38-point move and the typical Vermont county's 37. Nationally, most counties moved the other way, with a typical shift of 14 points to the left. Rutland, the most similar county, moved 36 points.

Turnout was 80% of the 2024 vote, 21,315 ballots against 26,552, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

50013.t:
Grand Isle County swung harder toward the Republicans than any other county in Vermont. Kamala Harris carried it by 21 points in 2024, but in the governor's race Phil Scott beat Amanda Janoo 2,720 to 1,495, a 29-point Republican margin. That is a move of 50 points, against 38 statewide and a typical 37 across Vermont's 14 counties, none of which moved left. Similar counties moved less: Orange and Caledonia about 33 points each, Bennington 29. Nationally, most counties moved toward the Democrats.

With all of the expected vote counted, 4,278 ballots were cast, 86% of the 2024 total. Because turnout fell, the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

50005.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Caledonia County swung from a 12-point Harris win in 2024 to a 20-point win for Republican Phil Scott over Democrat Amanda Janoo, who took 5,376 votes to Scott's 8,151. That 33-point move toward the Republicans is a little smaller than the typical Vermont county's 37 points. Every one of the state's 14 counties moved right, while nationally 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left. Neighbors with similar 2024 votes moved alike: Orange 33 points, Bennington 29 and Rutland 36.

Turnout was 13,832, or 84% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

50025.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Windham County stayed Democratic, backing Janoo over Scott 12,661 to 8,363, a 20-point margin, while Scott carried the state by 7. That is a 23-point shift toward the Republicans from Harris's 43-point margin in 2024, yet it was the smallest rightward move among Vermont's 14 counties, where the typical county swung 37 points. Similar counties moved much further: Washington swung 42 points to a near tie, and Addison and Windsor flipped narrowly to Scott.

Windham cast 21,420 votes, 83% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, most counties moved the other way, toward the Democrats.

50001.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Addison County went from backing Harris by 36 points in 2024 to backing Scott, the Republican, over Janoo, the Democrat, by 3 points, 10,016 votes to 9,487. That is a 39-point move toward the Republicans and a flip from Democratic to Republican, with all of the expected vote counted.

The swing ran with the state, not against it. Vermont as a whole moved 38 points right as Scott won by 7, and none of its 14 counties moved left. The typical one shifted 37 points. Similar counties split: Windsor flipped by a near-identical margin, Lamoille swung further right and Windham stayed Democratic. Nationally, most counties moved left. Turnout was 88% of 2024's, at 19,745 votes, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

50007.t: Chittenden County, Vermont's largest by votes cast, stayed Democratic in the race for governor but by far less than in 2024. Janoo carried it over Scott 44,438 to 38,857, a margin of 7 points, down from Harris's 54-point margin over Trump. That 47-point swing toward the Republicans was larger than the state's 38-point move and ranks 12th of 14 counties. No Vermont county moved left, while nationally most counties shifted toward the Democrats, typically by 14 points. Comparable counties also swung right: Washington by 42 points, Windsor by 38 and Windham by 23. Turnout was 84,113 votes, 87% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. All expected votes are counted.

50023.t:
In the race for Vermont governor, Washington County went from a 43-point Harris win in 2024 to a 1-point edge for Democrat Janoo over Republican Scott, 15,501 votes to 15,149. That is a 42-point move toward the Republicans, a little more than the state's 38-point swing and the typical Vermont county's 37. All 14 counties moved right, while nationally most moved left, typically by 14 points. Among similar counties, Windham shifted far less (23 points), while Windsor and Addison moved about as much and flipped to Scott.

With all of the expected vote counted, 31,092 ballots were cast, 89% of the 2024 total. The count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

50009.t:
In the governor's race, Essex County gave Republican Phil Scott 1,807 votes to Democrat Amanda Janoo's 665, a margin of about 44 points. Donald Trump carried the county by 16 points in 2024, so it moved 28 points toward the Republicans. All of the expected vote is counted.

Every Vermont county swung right as Scott won statewide by 7 points in a state Kamala Harris carried by 32. Essex, the state's smallest county by votes cast, moved less than the typical county's 37 points. Similar counties shifted more: Orleans by 32 points and Franklin by 39. Turnout was 2,580 votes, 76% of the 3,410 cast in 2024. The count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

50019.t: In the race for Vermont governor, Orleans County went for Phil Scott (R) over Amanda Janoo (D), 7,577 votes to 3,700, a Republican margin of 33 points. In 2024 Trump had carried it by just 2 points, so the county moved 32 points toward the Republicans. That is a large swing, but a little smaller than the typical Vermont county's 37-point move. No county in the state moved left, while nationally most counties did. Similar counties swung slightly harder, with Franklin moving 39 points, Rutland 36 and Caledonia 33. Turnout was 79% of the 2024 vote, 11,605 ballots against 14,655, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

50017.t:
Orange County voted for Harris by 20 points in 2024, then backed Republican Phil Scott over Democrat Amanda Janoo for governor, 8,258 to 6,341, a 13-point Republican margin and a 33-point move to the right. With all of the expected vote counted, about 14,890 ballots were cast, 85% of the 2024 total. Because turnout fell, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

The shift matched the state, not the country. Every one of Vermont's 14 counties moved right, typically by 37 points, while most counties nationally moved left. Orange ranks sixth in the state by size of move. Similar counties also flipped: Bennington moved 29 points and Caledonia 33, while Grand Isle swung 50.
